title: Generic pipes and stdio graduation
goal: Graduate pipes and nontrivial stdio from refused frontier resources into explicit generic resource graph classes only when stdio policy, pipe peer graph, producer/consumer lifecycle, no-hidden-shell-state boundaries, partial/unknown pipe refusal, and target-native reconstruction are proven with local matrix evidence.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove the pipes/stdio product contract is documented, including exact supported shapes, refused shapes, non-goals, target-native reconstruction rules, and explicit non-claims for arbitrary shell pipeline, PTY, terminal, or process teleportation.
proofChecklist.evidence: Documented the pipes/stdio product contract in docs/snapshot/generic-pipes-stdio-graduation.md and linked it from docs/snapshot/generic-resource-graph-frontier.md and docs/snapshot/README.md. The doc defines supported pilot shapes (finite pipe replay, long-running producer/consumer pair, and explicit nontrivial stdio policy), refused shapes (PTYs/terminals, hidden shell state, missing peers, fan-in/fan-out/cycles, partial/unknown kernel pipe buffers, blocked reads/writes without lifecycle, unknown anon inodes/sockets/devices/locks, nontrivial inherited stdio), descriptor taxonomy, target-native loader strategy, target evidence, non-goals, and graduation rule. Explicit non-claims include arbitrary shell pipeline movement, arbitrary shell command reconstruction, PTY/editor/session restoration, source-ISA emulation, memory/register continuation, and metadata-only success. Validation passed: pnpm run build:docs in 1.975s after formatting the docs.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove public or internal descriptor fields exist for stdio policy and pipe peer graph, including fd number, direction, flags, close-on-exec, nonblocking state, peer process identity, producer/consumer roles, peer inside/outside moved graph, and buffered-data policy.
proofChecklist.evidence: Added optional stdioGraph and pipeGraph descriptor fields to MoveGenericResourceGraphState in packages/runtime/src/move-pid-graph.ts. stdioGraph carries policy, fd 0/1/2 target, access, and evidence. pipeGraph carries pipes with inode, readFds/writeFds endpoints, endpoint pid/fd/role/insideMovedGraph/flags/cloexec/nonblocking/command/argv, topology, bufferedDataPolicy, and lifecycle. Updated packages/runtime/src/__tests__/move-generic-resource-graph-state.test.ts to prove the move descriptor capture surface can carry a modeled stdin pipe with one producer and one consumer, explicit stdio fd policies, topology=one-producer-one-consumer, bufferedDataPolicy=empty, and lifecycle=long-running-pair. Validation passed: NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG=/dev/null npx vitest run packages/runtime/src/__tests__/move-generic-resource-graph-state.test.ts, 1 file / 2 tests in 0.561s; pnpm -F @machinen/runtime build passed in 1.542s; pnpm run build:docs passed in 1.836s and regenerated packages/runtime/API.md.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove capture/classification distinguishes trivial stdio (/dev/null or closed), inherited noninteractive stdio, anonymous pipes, named FIFOs, shell pipelines, missing peers, fan-in/fan-out, partial/unknown pipe state, and unsupported PTY/terminal cases with exact resource-class evidence.
proofChecklist.evidence: Implemented descriptor-only stdio/pipe graph capture/classification in packages/cli/src/move-generic-resource-graph.ts without enabling pipe loader support. buildMoveGenericResourceGraphState now emits stdioGraph and pipeGraph. stdioGraph distinguishes /dev/null-or-closed, modeled-pipe, inherited-noninteractive, and refused stdio targets for fd 0/1/2. pipeGraph groups pipe:[inode] endpoints, records pid/fd/role/insideMovedGraph/flags/command/argv, topology one-producer-one-consumer/fan-in/fan-out/missing-peer, bufferedDataPolicy=refused-unknown, and lifecycle=refused. Focused tests in packages/cli/src/__tests__/move-generic-resource-graph.test.ts prove trivial /dev/null stdio, pipe stdin/stdout graph, one-producer-one-consumer topology, fan-in topology, missing-peer topology, named FIFO-like unknown-resource refusal, inherited-noninteractive stdio refusal, PTY refusal, and existing pipe/socket/anon-inode/device/active TCP refusal classes. proofChecklist.obligation: Prove producer/consumer lifecycle rules are explicit and implemented or refused: finite producer replay, long-running producer/consumer pairs, EOF/shutdown behavior, partial writes, blocked reads/writes, process exit ordering, and cleanup on failure.
proofChecklist.evidence: Producer/consumer lifecycle rules are currently explicit and fail-closed rather than accepted. docs/snapshot/generic-pipes-stdio-graduation.md defines finite replay, long-running producer/consumer pairs, EOF/shutdown, partial writes, blocked reads/writes, exit ordering, and cleanup requirements before support can graduate. The descriptor-only implementation records every observed pipe with bufferedDataPolicy=refused-unknown and lifecycle=refused until a target-native pipe loader proves a supported lifecycle. Focused tests assert pipeGraph entries for one-producer-one-consumer, fan-in, and missing-peer topologies all carry bufferedDataPolicy=refused-unknown and lifecycle=refused, and refusalClasses still include pipe/stdio so save/load remains fail-closed for pipe graphs. Same focused test command passed 2 files / 11 tests in 0.591s.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove no hidden shell state is accepted: shell wrappers, pipelines with unmodeled commands, job control, traps, expansions, shell variables, and PTY-backed interactive shells remain refused unless separately modeled and proven.
proofChecklist.evidence: Implemented hidden shell-state refusal in packages/cli/src/move-generic-resource-graph.ts. classifyGenericResourceGraph now sees the MovePidGraphNode and appends a shellState refusal when command is a shell wrapper (sh/dash/bash/zsh/fish/busybox with -c), preventing shell pipelines, traps, expansions, job-control-like wrappers, or hidden shell variables from being accepted as generic pipe/stdio support. Focused test packages/cli/src/__tests__/move-generic-resource-graph.test.ts proves sh -c "printf hi | grep h" records refusalClasses/resourceClasses with resourceClass=shellState and reason=shell wrapper state is not a generic pipe/stdio resource graph. Validation passed: focused tests 2 files / 12 tests in 0.575s; @machinen/cli build passed in 0.347s.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove a target-native loader strategy exists for the first supported pipe/stdio shape, including preflight gates, fd reconstruction, process launch order, health/target evidence, no target pid before gates pass, and cleanup on failure.
proofChecklist.evidence: Implemented first target-native pipe/stdio loader strategy in packages/cli/src/move-generic-resource-graph.ts behind explicit supported pipeGraph lifecycle fields. genericResourceGraphLoaderCommand now adds pipeGraph preflight before launch, supports finite-replay by creating a target-native shell pipeline that decodes capturedBytesBase64 and pipes bytes into the target-native consumer, and supports long-running-pair by validating a target-native producer argv before creating a target-native producer | consumer pipeline. The command initializes aux_pids and probe_fail kills the launched pipeline pid plus any auxiliary pid list on failure. Focused tests prove preflight precedes pipe launch, LOAD_PID appears only after launch, finite replay uses base64 -d piped into the consumer, long-running pair validates producer executable before launch and pipes producer argv into the consumer, and cleanup includes kill -TERM "$pid" $aux_pids. Validation passed before matrix proof: focused tests 2 files / 13 tests in 0.643s and CLI build in 0.369s. Final matrix proof after preflight refactor passed at /tmp/machinen-move-matrix-10330-1781216492.

stopIf: The implementation would claim arbitrary shell pipeline, PTY, terminal, or process teleportation without modeling every observed resource.
The implementation cannot distinguish hidden shell state from explicit pipe graph state.
The implementation would accept partial buffered data, missing peers, fan-in/fan-out, blocked reads/writes, or nontrivial inherited stdio without exact support proof.
The implementation would launch target processes before pipe/stdio preflight gates pass.
The implementation would weaken existing generic refusal evidence or bespoke fallback priority before equivalent proof exists.
Required local proof tooling or VMM assets are unavailable for the targeted matrix rows.
Required validation fails and cannot be fixed within the pipes/stdio scope.
The /goal loop reaches 8 agent completion(s) without satisfying the contract.
